newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli defence chief expects Syrian talks soon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli defence chief expects Syrian talks soon.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said in remarks broadcast on Friday that he expected Israelis and Syrians to meet soon to revive their deadlocked peace talks.

"To the best of my understanding...around spring, after the U.S. administration is established, there will be a meeting in which we and the Syrians must look for ways to bridge some of the gaps," he said on Israel Radio.
On-again, off-again peace talks that began in 1991 have been stuck over the fate of the Golan Heights captured by Israel from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war.

Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy appealed on Wednesday to his Syrian counterpart, Farouq al-Shara, to meet to resuscitate the U.S.-brokered talks. Levy said he was exchanging messages with Damascus.
Mordechai, who was speaking on Thursday night, said he hoped to reach a dialogue with Damascus that would reduce the threats and dangers -- even if it did not bring about the peace Israel wanted.

Israel's pullout from most of the West Bank town of Hebron last week has prompted renewed interest in the long-stalled talks with Damascus. U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk appealed to Syria to use Hebron as a springboard.

Israeli-Syrian tensions escalated following the election in May of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who rejects Syria's demand that Israel return the strategic plateau that towers over both countries.

Army chief Lieutenant-General Amnon Shahak, in remarks also broadcast by the radio, said his troops had not been on alert in the Golan Heights at any time in recent months. He said there was no immediate danger of war -- but that could change.

"I don't know that I can promise myself or you that in a longer process which could take months or more that Syria won't reach the conclusion that for its own reasons it's worthwhile to initiate a military action against Israel," he said.
Israel's previous Labour-led government, ousted by Netanyahu, broke off talks with Syria in March 1996 after Islamic suicide bombings in Israel killed 59 people.
